topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
response: Interleaved array element spacing affects coverage patterns by mitigating grating lobes. For Ka-band satellite links, an element spacing of ≤ 0.6λ (where λ is the wavelength) suppresses grating lobes, ensuring efficient beamforming and minimizing interference.
reference_context: Multibeam satellite systems use multiple antennae to increase coverage gain, allocating the same spectrum to serve more users, but face challenges like interference among beams and inter-cell interference.
